text:
maria: quick update — I brought up cyclotron14b (int4) on a small fleet of v2 nodes this morning. initial bench looks promising for throughput but we have two issues: 1) a measurable quality regression on the summarization eval (ROUGE-1 down ~1.8%), 2) memory fragmentation spikes under sustained batching which led to OOMs at higher batch sizes. posting numbers and a proposed config below.

josh: can you drop the perf tables + exact OOM stack traces? also which quant scheme did you use? :thinking_face:

maria: perf summary link: https://redwood.internal/bench/1711213141 (private). short numbers: p50 gen latency 110ms -> 105ms (per-channel vs baseline per-tensor), p95 420ms -> 390ms, throughput +8% tokens/sec. QA rouge-1: baseline fp16 0.524, int4 per-tensor 0.519, int4 per-channel 0.514. memory: resident peaks +18% variance; gradual free-list fragmentation after ~7000 requests, then slab failures at batch >=12 for seq_len ~512. OOM trace (snippet):
```
[ 2024-11-22 09:32:11 ] CUDA OOM at alloc 512MB in slab_allocator.cpp:234
KV cache resize triggered, failed at attempt 3
prefetch_pool exhausted
```

maria: current canary config I used:
```yaml
model: cyclotron14b-int4
image: redwood/runtime:v2.7.1
quant:
  scheme: per_channel
  calib: act_range
batching:
  min_batch: 1
  target_batch: 6
  max_batch: 12
defaults:
  max_tokens: 256
  generation_window: 64
  slot_reserve_fraction: 0.06
eviction:
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.65
  early_kv_evict: false
```

emily: thanks. the quality hit is non-trivial for summarization. can we run an A/B eval (fp16 vs int4 per-channel) over the standard summarization suite and quantify user-facing deltas (rouge, compression ratio, hallucination rate)? If regression > 1.0% we should rollback int4 or reduce aggressiveness. also consider lowering target_batch to 4 as a mitigation.

josh: agree on the AB test. two infra mitigations we can try in parallel: 1) toggle early_kv_evict: true to free long-tail KV entries more aggressively, 2) increase slot_reserve_fraction to 0.12 for the canary, 3) enable a lightweight compaction job that runs every 5 minutes to defrag the free list. these should reduce fragmentation spikes.

qa-bot: smoke tests started for canary variants (fp16 / int4-per-channel). ETA ~ 18m. logs: https://redwood.internal/ci/1711213141/logs

maria: I also reran quant calibration with per-channel but lower clip_percentile (98 -> 95) and saw a small quality recovery (~+0.6 ROUGE) but throughput dropped ~1.5%. posting config tweak:
```yaml
quant:
  scheme: per_channel
  clip_percentile: 95
```

emily: that tradeoff looks worth exploring if it fixes hallucination regressions. but we should avoid permanent defaults that slow down latency too much. propose this rollout plan:
- short AB run (12h) on 1% traffic for int4-per-channel w/ clip95 + slot_reserve 12% + early_kv_evict true
- runway metrics: rouge-1, hallucination-rate, p95 latency, OOM count
- rollback rule: rouge-1 drop > 1.0% OR OOM_count >= 1 in the canary window

josh: minor ask — add an automatic fallback route in routing policy so that if the canary node hits OOM we reroute to cyclotron14b-fp16 variant instead of failing requests. config snippet:
```json
{"fallback": {"on_oom": "cyclotron14b-fp16", "priority":"regional"}}
```

maria: will implement the routing fallback and kick off the AB. starting the canary with lowered target_batch=4 and slot_reserve_fraction=0.12 now. will post results. :thumbsup:

qa-bot: canary A/B launched (1% traffic). variants: fp16 (control), int4-per-channel-clip95 (candidate). monitoring: perf, eval-scores, OOM alerts.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary window for 1711213141 — start 2024-11-22T10:00Z, end 2024-11-22T22:00Z.

josh: couple of follow-ups after canary: if fragmentation persists, we should consider adding a periodic GPU defrag job that forces a small warmup pattern to stabilize allocator freelist, and think about a soft throttle that caps batch assembly when free list fragmentation > X.

maria: noted. action items: (1) run AB and post detailed metric table, (2) enable fallback route & early_kv_evict, (3) if AB fails, revert int4 for summarization route and open a postmortem on quant calibration.

emily: thanks — please ping #eng-ml-alerts if canary trips any of the rollback rules.

maria: will do. thanks all.
